pairs.right: Is somebody doing something bad now?
What is wrong with the configuration?

right_distractors: How much does the account spend?

prompt: What does GuardDuty need installed on instances to read VPC Flow Logs and DNS queries?
hint: It reads logs AWS already has.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right. Turning the detector on is enough.

choices.text: An agent on every instance
choices.why: Runtime monitoring uses an agent; the foundational sources do not.

choices.text: Flow logs turned on in each VPC first
choices.why: GuardDuty reads its own copy without them being enabled.

choices.text: A Security Hub subscription
choices.why: GuardDuty works on its own.

prompt: Why does Security Hub's aggregation matter to a small team?

choices.text: It makes the findings disappear faster
choices.why: It gathers them; it does not resolve them.

choices.text: It replaces GuardDuty and Inspector
choices.why: They still produce the findings.

choices.text: It costs less than the two services together
choices.why: It is priced on top of them.

choices.text: One queue in one format instead of three to watch
choices.why: Right. ASFF, read in one place.

prompt: What does the finding type UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS say?

choices.text: An IAM user's password was guessed from outside AWS
choices.why: It is about an instance's temporary credentials, not a password.

choices.text: An instance's credentials were used outside AWS
choices.why: Right. Somebody else holds them now.

choices.text: An instance sent data to an address outside AWS
choices.why: That would be an exfiltration of data, a different family.

choices.text: Root credentials were used from a new country
choices.why: Root usage has its own Policy finding.

prompt: From what severity number does GuardDuty call a finding high?
The office's scanner probes the shop every night. Which suppression filter does the lesson recommend?

choices.text: Archive every Recon finding
choices.why: That hides real probes from anybody.

choices.text: Disable GuardDuty at night
choices.why: Attackers work at night too.

choices.text: Probe type plus scanner address
choices.why: Right. Type and address together.

choices.text: Lower every finding's severity to low
choices.why: A filter archives; it does not rewrite severity.

prompt: On AWS, the command that makes one example finding of every type, to test the route to a phone, is aws guardduty create-____-findings. (one word)
A get-findings filter on CRITICAL returned all six findings in the lab. What does that say?

choices.text: All six are critical
choices.why: The list before showed HIGH, LOW and MEDIUM too.

choices.text: The filter's syntax was wrong for the command line
choices.why: It is AWS's documented syntax.

choices.text: Security Hub filters only by product
choices.why: It filters by dozens of fields.

choices.text: moto ignores get-findings filters
choices.why: Right. AWS applies them.

prompt: Match each ASFF field to what it holds.
hint: Who, what kind, how bad, about what.

pairs.right: Its place in a three-level taxonomy

prompt: What workflow status does a new finding have on AWS?

choices.text: ACTIVE
choices.why: That is the record state, a different field.

choices.text: OPEN
choices.why: Not an ASFF status.

choices.text: NEW
choices.why: Right. Then NOTIFIED, SUPPRESSED or RESOLVED.

choices.text: None, as moto showed
choices.why: moto sets none; AWS sets NEW.

prompt: Put the lesson's three triage questions in the order they are asked.
items: Is there a known, published way in?

prompt: Why did triage.py put a HIGH finding above two CRITICAL ones?
hint: Severity is how bad it would be.

choices.text: It sorts alphabetically by title
choices.why: It sorts by tier, then severity.

choices.text: It is happening now
choices.why: Right. Every hour it waits, somebody else has the credentials.

choices.text: GuardDuty findings always come first
choices.why: The LOW GuardDuty finding came last.

choices.text: HIGH ranks above CRITICAL in ASFF
choices.why: CRITICAL is the higher label.

prompt: Two critical CVEs: one with a published exploit in the api image, one without in a build tool. Why does the lesson treat them differently?

choices.text: One of them has a ready-made attack
choices.why: Right. Tier 2, two days; the other waits for tier 3.

choices.text: Build tools are never a risk
choices.why: They are, just less urgently here.

choices.text: Inspector scored them differently by mistake
choices.why: Both were labelled CRITICAL.

choices.text: The api image is larger
choices.why: Size has nothing to do with it.

prompt: shop-exports, a public bucket, landed in tier 3. What should move it to the top?

choices.text: Its severity label being HIGH
choices.why: It already was HIGH, and stayed in tier 3.

choices.text: Its name containing the word exports
choices.why: A name is not evidence of content.

choices.text: A second finding about the same bucket
choices.why: A duplicate adds no information.

choices.text: Learning that it holds the customers' exports
choices.why: Right. Then it is a leak in progress.
